_comment: DK CAD Mobile release manifest. Lives in the dk_cad Pages repo ROOT as mobile-update.json; the app reads it from https://dheerajkum7g7-eng.github.io/dk_cad/mobile-update.json with the raw.githubusercontent copy as a mirror. The APK is stored as 2 MB PARTS because the publishing network's proxy rejects large authenticated uploads; GitHub does not join them, mobile.html does. To ship a new build: run publish-mobile.ps1, which rewrites version/size/sha256/partCount here. Keep this file SEPARATE from the desktop's update.json.
_urlNote: The SAME release asset the Google Sites download button points at, so there is one download in the world, not two. Release MV / DKCadMobile.apk is replaced in place on every version - the website link never changes. mobile.html on Pages is a BACKUP route for networks where github.com is blocked (this office's own laptops get 403 there).
notes: THREE FIXES, ALL OF THEM THINGS THAT WASTED YOUR TIME ON SITE. UPDATE NOTICE IS INSTANT: the check for a new version used to start only after the whole app had finished loading, and then asked each server one after the other, so the notice could arrive ten or fifteen seconds in - by which time you had already opened a drawing in the old build and stopped looking. It now starts on the very first instruction of a launch, while the screen is still being built, and asks every server at the same time, so it is there as soon as the app is. It still only appears on a fresh start, never when you come back to the app from something else. GPS THAT IS SWITCHED OFF NOW SAYS SO: giving the app permission and having the phone's location actually turned on are two different switches, and the app only ever checked the first. With permission granted but the phone's GPS off, every position path failed silently and Locate simply sat on waiting for a GPS fix forever, with nothing on screen to tell you why. It now notices, says exactly what is wrong, and takes you straight to the setting to turn it on. LOCATE NO LONGER STARTS FROM AN OLD POSITION: the first position shown was whatever the phone last recorded, with no check of how old it was - it could be this morning, or another town - so Locate pointed somewhere wrong for ten to fifteen seconds and then jumped. A remembered position is now only used while it is still seconds old and accurate; otherwise the app goes and gets a real fix at full accuracy. When there is genuinely nothing recent, it says waiting for a GPS fix, which is true, instead of showing a confident wrong number. PREVIOUS RELEASE (5.4): Local to UTM alignment and the background map, described below.
_notes54: TWO NEW THINGS IN THIS RELEASE. LOCAL TO UTM: a drawing on a local site grid (starting at 0,0 or 1000,1000) states nothing about where it is on Earth, so the app has never been able to give it a latitude and longitude. Now it can - if you tell it where the drawing is. Open a local drawing and a Local to UTM button appears at the bottom. It can read the drawing's OWN written coordinate labels and work the position out by itself, and it takes each coordinate from the survey marker or the leader ARROWHEAD the label points at, never from the text box, which on a survey sheet routinely sits tens of metres away from the point it describes. Every label is cross-checked against the others and any that disagree are thrown out, so one typo cannot tilt the answer. If the drawing carries no written coordinates you can pick two points and type what they really are; a third is offered, because it is the first point that can CHECK the other two. Nothing is applied until you have seen the rotation, the scale and the error it fits with, and the alignment is remembered for that drawing. BACKGROUND MAP: a new Map button puts satellite imagery, a road map or a topographic map BEHIND your drawing, lined up with the real world - so your lines sit on the ground they were surveyed from. One tap cycles Satellite, Road, Topo and off. It stays off until you switch it on, and it never switches itself on again, not even for the next drawing. It ASKS which UTM zone the drawing is in instead of assuming the zone you happen to be standing in, and it shows you where that zone puts the drawing so a wrong one is obvious before you accept it. Zooming in deeply no longer leaves blank tiles: where the imagery for your area runs out, the closest level that does exist is stretched instead, so the map is never white. Tiles are cached on the phone, so panning back over ground you have already seen costs no data. On a local drawing the map asks you to convert to UTM first and takes you straight to that tool. Imagery credit: Esri, Maxar, Earthstar Geographics. Road map by OpenStreetMap contributors. PREVIOUS RELEASE (5.1): absolute CAD text heights, snapping in the UTM picker, and far more reliable detection of georeferenced drawings.
_notes51: Label height is now an absolute value in drawing units. The box in the bottom bar opens at exactly 1.0 in every drawing and accepts any value from 0.0001 to 100 - it is no longer derived from the drawing's extents, so it will not open at 730 in one file and 0.0075 in another, and there is no per-drawing minimum to get stuck against. The coordinate leader no longer flips sides while zooming: the direction is fixed at the moment the point is picked. The UTM picker now snaps - endpoints, midpoints, intersections, nodes and geometry inside blocks - and its panel shows the drawing's own X,Y, the UTM easting/northing with the zone and MGRS band letter (for example 43Q) worked out from the point itself, and the WGS84 latitude and longitude. Detection of georeferenced drawings is far more reliable: it is now decided by a vote of the geometry rather than by the centre of the bounding box, so a single stray object at the origin no longer causes a valid survey to be reported as a local drawing. A genuinely local drawing is labelled Local Coordinate and is given no UTM zone at all.
_notes50: See where you are ON the drawing. Press the new GPS button and a blue dot marks your own position on the plan, with a circle showing how accurate the fix is - and it moves as you walk, like Google Maps. It works on any georeferenced drawing anywhere in the world: the UTM zone and hemisphere are worked out from your own position, nothing is fixed to one country. On a local site grid it says so rather than placing you somewhere wrong. The UTM panel also gains a Here button, which drops your current position into the coordinate list and copies its Easting/Northing and latitude/longitude straight to the clipboard. The coordinate and distance labels are CAD text again: the box in the bottom bar is now a HEIGHT IN DRAWING UNITS, so type 1 on a metre survey and the label is one metre tall - it grows and shrinks with the drawing as you zoom instead of sitting over it. Everything from 4.9 - the UTM point picker, snapping inside blocks, the INS snap and the slim three-row toolbar - is unchanged.
